title: Flow Cytometry Pipeline for Rapid Quantification of C2C12 Cell Differentiation
author: Parisi, Sünnen, et al.
materials: This part is optional and can be applied to investigate the impact of disease variant genes of interest and the gene dose on C2C12 cell differentiation. It can be combined with drug treatments to furthermore assess a drug’s effect on the transiently genetically altered C2C12 cells (part 4). C2C12 cell transfection with a GFP-variant tagged gene of interest can be performed once the cells have reached 50%–60% confluency. Alternatively, a construct coexpressing a GFP-variant using an IRES-element or P2A-autocleavage sequence may be employed, however, this approach may require additional validations (see Expected outcomes section).

In this part, we describe how to perform the manual analysis of the acquired flow cytometry data using the GuavaSoft 4.0 Software to quantify the percentage of differentiated cells in target samples. Timing: ∼15 min for first time users; ∼5 min thereafter

We developed here FlowFate as a free, interactive R-based analysis software program that automates the quantitation of GFP-variant expressing C2C12 cell differentiation data as obtained by flow cytometry. Thus, it may be suitable for medium-throughput screening.

FlowFate can read flow cytometry data stored in flow cytometry standard (FCS) 3.0 format that originate from either single tube or 96-well plate acquisitions. Samples collected from a standard 96-well plate will be displayed by default with the corresponding well number. Prior to analysis, users should take note of the well numbers for each sample e.g., well A01 for double-negative sample etc.

FlowFate was developed by combining existing R packages (flowCore and flowWorkspace for FCS file import, data manipulation and gating, and ggcyto for visualization) into a customized workflow tailored to the analysis of differentiation data. FlowFate can quantify differentiated cells in up to three GFP-expression bins, thus enabling analysis of the gene dose-dependent effect of GFP-variant tagged/ coexpressing genes of interest. In the following, we employ as such a GFP-variant mEGFP.
First, the user has to perform the instrument set up essentially as described in part 6.

In FlowFate we have then eliminated manual gating steps by using pre-defined settings to exclude debris (Figure S4B) and identify GFP+ cells during the ‘Curate’ step. GFP-thresholding is achieved by utilizing the ‘quantile gate’ from openCyto. Quantile gates are used to determine a threshold below which 99% of cells are found. This GFP-threshold value is obtained by averaging the GFP-channel data from the double-negative and MyHC+ control samples analogous to what was described in part 6, as depicted in Figure S4C. The GFP-threshold is then applied to all samples during the ‘curation’ step to analyze only GFP+ events. It also sets the lower limit of the GFP-low bin. To examine the gene dose-dependent effect of the GFP-variant tagged/ coexpressing gene of interest, up to three GFP-expression bins can be defined (GFP-low, -medium and -high).

The ‘Split peaks’ command automatically plots histograms of the MyHC-channel within each user-specified GFP-bin for every sample. We use a ‘peak-splitting’ algorithm from openCyto, which determines the intersection point between two population peaks and automatically creates a gate including intensities above this cutpoint (the cutpoint is depicted as a red line in Figure S5D). The two distinct subpopulations are MyHC- (intensity peak on the left of the red line) and MyHC+ (intensity peak on the right of the red line) (Figure S5D). steps.title: Prepare high- and low-serum media
steps.instruction: Prepare C2C12 growth medium containing 10 % fetal bovine serum (high serum) and differentiation medium containing 2 % horse serum (low serum) according to the recipes listed in the Materials and Equipment section; solutions may be made fresh or stored as described.

steps.title: Culture C2C12 cells to confluence
steps.instruction: Seed C2C12 myoblasts in high‑serum medium and grow until they reach approximately 90 % confluency (≈3 × 10⁵ cells per well of a 6‑well plate).

steps.title: Induce differentiation in low serum
steps.instruction: Replace high‑serum medium with low‑serum differentiation medium (2 % horse serum) and incubate for 3 days; after this period the late differentiation marker myosin heavy chain (MyHC) will be expressed.

steps.title: Optional transfect with GFP‑variant plasmid
steps.instruction: When cells are 50‑60 % confluent, transfect with a GFP‑variant‑tagged construct using jetPRIME (or an alternative reagent) as follows:

substeps.instruction: Dilute 2 µg plasmid DNA in 200 µL jetPRIME buffer; vortex briefly.
Vortex the jetPRIME reagent for 5 s and spin down.
Add 4 µL jetPRIME reagent to the DNA solution, vortex, and spin down.
Incubate the transfection mix for 10 min at 22‑25 °C.
Add 200 µL of the transfection mix dropwise to each well containing 2 mL growth medium; distribute evenly.
After 4 h, replace the medium with fresh high‑serum medium.

steps.title: Optional drug treatment after transfection
steps.instruction: Four hours post‑transfection, add the desired drug or vehicle to the culture (e.g., 0.2 % DMSO as control or 3 µM AMG 510). Continue incubation in low‑serum medium for the remainder of the 3‑day differentiation period.

steps.title: Acquire flow cytometry data
steps.instruction: Collect cells after the 3‑day differentiation period, prepare single‑cell suspensions, and acquire data on a flow cytometer; save files in FCS 3.0 format (single‑tube or 96‑well plate layout).

steps.title: Manual analysis with GuavaSoft
steps.instruction: Using GuavaSoft 4.0, manually quantify MyHC‑positive cells as follows:

substeps.instruction: Implement basic gate settings from part 6 (debris exclusion, double‑negative control).
Open the ‘QuadStat Marker’ window and draw four quadrants; position the marker at approximately 10¹ on both axes.
Add a ‘New Stat’ with the ‘Count’ metric to obtain event numbers for each quadrant.
Define GFP‑low bin as 101‑102 RFU in the Green‑B channel; GFP‑medium as 102‑103 RFU; GFP‑high as 103‑104 RFU.
Within each GFP bin, classify cells as MyHC‑positive if the Red‑R channel signal exceeds the ~101 threshold (set using the double‑negative sample).
Export the counts of MyHC⁺ and MyHC⁻ cells for each bin, calculate the percentage of MyHC⁺ cells relative to the total GFP‑low population, and plot the results (e.g., in Excel).

steps.title: Install R, RStudio, and FlowFate
steps.instruction: Set up the software environment required for automated analysis:

substeps.instruction: Download and install R from https://posit.co/download/rstudio-desktop/ (install R before RStudio).
Launch RStudio and create a new R script.
Run: install.packages(c("remotes", "BiocManager"))
Run: BiocManager::install(c("ggcyto", "flowWorkspace", "flowCore")) and answer ‘a’ to update all packages.
Run: remotes::install_github("RGLab/openCyto") and answer ‘1’ to any update prompts.
Run: remotes::install_github("maximesunnen/flowFate@*release") and answer ‘1’ when prompted.
Installation needs to be performed only once; check the GitHub page for newer releases.

steps.title: Run FlowFate automated analysis
steps.instruction: Analyze the FCS files with FlowFate as follows:

substeps.instruction: In RStudio, execute flowFate::run_app() to launch the web‑based app.
Click ‘Open in Browser’, then choose the data format (single merged FCS file or folder of individual FCS files) and upload the files.

Select the GFP channel (e.g., GRN.B.HLin) and MyHC channel (e.g., RED.R.HLin) in the ‘Curate’ tab; start curation to apply the pre‑defined debris gate and GFP‑threshold derived from double‑negative and MyHC⁺ controls.
Add GFP bins: for example, GFP‑low 24.1‑100 RFU, GFP‑medium 101‑1000 RFU, GFP‑high 1001‑10000 RFU (the lower bound of GFP‑low equals the automatically set GFP‑threshold and should not be altered).
Optionally add additional bins for gene‑dose analysis.
Switch to the ‘Split peaks’ tab and click ‘Split’ to let the algorithm identify MyHC⁻ (left peak) and MyHC⁺ (right peak) subpopulations within each GFP bin.
Use the ‘Plot’ panel to visualise histograms and verify gating.
Click ‘Export’, then ‘Show population statistics’ to download a CSV containing sample name, population name, and event count.
Calculate the fraction of differentiated cells in each GFP bin by dividing the MyHC⁺ count (e.g., /NonDebris/GFP+/GFP‑low/MyHC+) by the total GFP‑low count (e.g., /NonDebris/GFP+/GFP‑low).
Repeat the calculation for all target samples and perform downstream statistical analysis as needed.

description: Cell differentiation is a fundamental process during development, but also highly relevant in regenerative research and for understanding the evolution of cancer and other diseases. Only a few in vitro models exist that faithfully recapitulate essential facets of cell differentiation as observed in vivo.2 The heterogeneous mouse muscle C2C12 myoblasts proliferate under high serum (10% fetal bovine serum) conditions.3 Upon switching to low serum (2% horse serum), a fraction of these cells differentiate and after typically 3 days the late differentiation marker myosin heavy chain (MyHC) is expressed.4 Using flow cytometry, we here quantify the fraction of cells that expresses MyHC as a measure of C2C12 cell differentiation. We describe how this assay can quantify the extent to which GFP-variant tagged disease mutants, in our case of the oncogene KRAS, impact differentiation. Gating for GFP-positive cells allows to analyze specifically the mutant expressing subpopulation in a gene-dose dependent manner. We furthermore demonstrate how drug treatments can rescue this aberrant activity. Both GFP-construct expression and drug treatments are optional and the flowchart of our step-by-step experimental and analysis pipeline illustrates these options (Figure 1A).Figure 1Overview of differentiation phenotype and analysis pipeline(A) Flowchart of experimental and analysis steps with part-numbering as applied in this protocol.(B) C2C12 cells at ∼90% confluency in high serum medium.(C) Differentiated myotubes after culturing cells in low serum medium for 3 days. Scale bar 200 μm (B, C). Our assay is the most quantitative assay of C2C12 cell differentiation to date and uniquely allows to measure the impact of transient genetic manipulations in combination with drug treatments at a single-cell level. It may thus emerge as an important new tool in cancer research that enables the analysis of the differentiation restoring activity of drugs, as compared to the common anti-proliferative
